scope_note: Round-2 increment only: new edges for SD/MU/SL; dated e-GDDS edges for IR/AF/YE/SY; replacements for the four flagged round-1 problems. Does not restate unchallenged round-1 edges.

SD.basis: IMF GDDS/e-GDDS metadata first posted 19 August 2003; no NSDP has been launched. GDDS participants automatically participate in e-GDDS after the 2015 successor framework.
SD.evidence_quote: Also, on August 19, 2003, Sudan formally began to participate in the IMF’s General Data Dissemination System (GDDS). On this date comprehensive information on its statistical production and dissemination practices were published on the IMF’s Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board.

SD.basis: IMF DSBB important-dates table still lists Sudan as an e-GDDS participant with metadata but no NSDP. This is a real, dated, still-listed obligation; it is not an active dissemination commitment at the NSDP threshold.
SD.evidence_quote: Sudan | August 19, 2003 |  [Date Metadata First Posted on the DSBB; Date e-GDDS NSDP First Posted is blank]

MU.basis: Graduated from GDDS (metadata first posted 21 September 2000) to SDDS on 28 February 2012 as the 70th subscriber; later upgraded to SDDS Plus on 16 March 2026. Target node reused is imf-sdds, the parent Data Standards Initiative tier named in both IMF press releases.
MU.evidence_quote: Mauritius subscribed today to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF’s) Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS), bringing the number of subscribing countries to 70. Mauritius is the 11th country to graduate to the SDDS from the IMF’s General Data Dissemination System (GDDS), which the country has participated in since September 21, 2000.

MU.basis: SDDS Plus is the highest tier of the same IMF Data Standards Initiatives. Included because it is the current live obligation as of March 2026.
MU.evidence_quote: Mauritius has adhered to the IMF’s Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) Plus, the highest tier of the IMF’s Data Standards Initiatives. It is the first country in Africa and the 32nd country globally to achieve this milestone in data transparency.

MU.basis: Statistics Mauritius told the UN National Accounts questionnaire that it switched compilation from 1993 SNA to 2008 SNA in June 2016.
MU.evidence_quote: The latest estimates presented in the following tables have been prepared in accordance with the concepts and definitions of the System of the National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA). In fact, Mauritius started the compilation of national accounts based on the 2008 SNA in June 2016. Previous estimates were according to the 1993 SNA.

SL.basis: GDDS metadata first posted 29 May 2003; e-GDDS NSDP first posted 8 December 2016. IMF press release confirms implementation of e-GDDS recommendations via an NSDP hosted by Statistics Sierra Leone, the Bank of Sierra Leone, and the Ministry of Finance.
SL.evidence_quote: Sierra Leone has implemented the recommendations of the Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS)—endorsed by the IMF Executive Board in May 2015—by disseminating a National Summary Data Page (NSDP). … The NSDP is posted on the websites of Statistics Sierra Leone, the Bank of Sierra Leone, and the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development

SL.basis: IMF DSBB important-dates table (opened) dates both the original metadata posting and the NSDP.

IQ.basis: Replacement for the round-1 ODIN third-party edge. Primary IMF sources: 15 December 2009 GDDS participation press release (CBI governor on the record) and the 2025 Article IV data-standards annex, which restates current e-GDDS status and the absence of an NSDP.
IQ.evidence_quote: The Republic of Iraq began participating today in the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF’s) General Data Dissemination System (GDDS), marking a major step forward in the development of its statistical system. … “Iraq is committed to use the IMF’s General Data Dissemination System as a general framework to continue developing the national statistical system consistent with best international practices,” Dr. Sinan Al-Shabibi, Governor of the Central Bank of Iraq, said.

IQ.basis: Current IMF staff assessment: participation is real but the recommended e-GDDS data dissemination (NSDP) has not been implemented. DSBB still hosts an Iraq e-GDDS contacts page.
IQ.evidence_quote: Iraq participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS) and first posted its metadata in December 2009 but is yet to disseminate the data recommended under the e-GDDS.

IR.basis: Dated, still-listed e-GDDS participation via metadata first posted 6 August 2012. No NSDP has ever been posted. Ninth Review chronology lists Iran as a 2012 GDDS participant. This is a lapsed-in-practice but officially still-recorded obligation, not a current active dissemination program.
IR.evidence_quote: Iran | August 6, 2012 |  [Date Metadata First Posted on the DSBB; Date e-GDDS NSDP First Posted is blank]

AF.basis: Dated GDDS/e-GDDS metadata first posted 22 June 2006; no NSDP. Contemporary IMF Board document (June 2006) recorded that STA had indicated Afghanistan would imminently become a GDDS participant. The DSBB listing remains; there is no IMF notice that the program was formally withdrawn.
AF.evidence_quote: Afghanistan, Islamic Republic of | June 22, 2006 |  [Date Metadata First Posted on the DSBB; Date e-GDDS NSDP First Posted is blank]

AF.basis: Contemporaneous IMF Executive Board document confirming the then-imminent GDDS participation.
AF.evidence_quote: In September 2004, with the assistance of international agencies, the authorities launched a statistics master plan to produce official statistics in line with international standards. Their efforts have borne fruits, and it is heartening to note that STA has indicated (since the publication of the staff report) that Afghanistan will imminently become a participant in the General Data Dissemination Standards (GDDS).

YE.basis: Dated GDDS/e-GDDS metadata first posted 26 April 2001; no NSDP. Ninth Review chronology lists the Republic of Yemen among 2001 GDDS participants. No IMF notice of formal withdrawal was found; the DSBB row is still there. This is a now-inactive dissemination practice, not a current NSDP.
YE.evidence_quote: Yemen, Republic of | April 26, 2001 |  [Date Metadata First Posted on the DSBB; Date e-GDDS NSDP First Posted is blank]

SY.basis: Dated GDDS/e-GDDS metadata first posted 12 December 2007; no NSDP. Ninth Review chronology lists the Syrian Arab Republic among 2007 GDDS participants. No IMF notice of formal withdrawal was found. Recorded obligation, not a current active NSDP.
SY.evidence_quote: Syrian Arab Republic | December 12, 2007 |  [Date Metadata First Posted on the DSBB; Date e-GDDS NSDP First Posted is blank]

ID.basis: Country-named, not the generic ACSS sentence. Indonesia is an ASEAN founding member (8 August 1967) and BPS chaired/hosted ACSS13 in Jakarta in 2023.
ID.evidence_quote: The Thirteenth Session of the ASEAN Community Statistical System Committee (ACSS13), hosted by BPS Statistics Indonesia, was held on 22 to 24 November 2023. The Session was chaired by Ms. Amalia Adininggar Widyasanti, Acting Chief Statistician of BPS Statistics Indonesia

ID.basis: ASEAN’s own official roster naming Indonesia as a founding member.
ID.evidence_quote: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was established on 8 August 1967. The Member States are Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Viet Nam.

PH.basis: Country-named: the Philippines is an ASEAN founding member and will hold the ACSS chair in 2026; PSA’s deputy national statistician co-chaired ACSS15.
PH.evidence_quote: The Fifteenth Session of the ASEAN Community Statistical System Committee (ACSS15), hosted by Department of Statistics Malaysia, was held on 3 to 5 November 2025. The Session was chaired by YBhg. Dato Sri Dr. Mohd Uzir Mahidin, Chief Statistician of Department of Statistics Malaysia, with Ms. Minerva Eloisa P. Esquivias, Deputy National Statistician of Philippine Statistics Authority as the Co-chairperson. … We welcomed the ACSS Chairship of the Philippines in 2026.

SG.basis: Clarification of the contradictory DOS wording. IMF’s own subscription table, opened at dsbb.imf.org/sdds/subscription-date, separates three dates. DOS’s phrase “met all SDDS requirements at the time of its subscription in January 2001” collapses two events: subscription was 1 August 1996; the date Singapore met the specifications was 30 January 2001.
SG.evidence_quote: Singapore | 1-Aug-1996 | 19-Sep-1996 | 30-Jan-2001  [Country | Date of Subscription | Date Metadata were Posted on the DSBB | Date when subscriber met SDDS specifications]

SG.basis: National office statement for the 1996 subscription date, kept because it is country-specific; the January 2001 clause on the same page is the wording that should not be treated as a second subscription date.
SG.evidence_quote: Singapore was among the first group of 34 countries to subscribe to the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) in August 1996. … Singapore met all SDDS requirements at the time of its subscription in January 2001.

SG.basis: Country-named: Singapore Department of Statistics hosted and chaired ACSS8 in 2018.
SG.evidence_quote: The Eighth Session of the ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) Committee, or ACSS8, hosted by the Singapore Department of Statistics, was held on 9 to 11 October 2018 in Singapore. … The Session was chaired by Ms. Wong Wee Kim, Chief Statistician of the Singapore Department of Statistics.

TH.basis: Country-named: Thailand is an ASEAN founding member; NSO Bangkok hosted ACSS9 in 2019, and a Thai NSO deputy director-general co-chaired ACSS8.
IMF SDDS subscription table names Thailand specifically (not needed for the ASEAN fix, included because the same official table was opened and is country-specific).

MM.basis: Country-named: Myanmar joined ASEAN on 23 July 1997; the Union of Myanmar is a named signatory of the ACSS Code of Practice; ACSS4 was hosted in Nay Pyi Taw.
MM.evidence_quote: We, the Heads of Statistical Offices of Brunei Darussalam, the Kingdom of Cambodia, the Republic of Indonesia, the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, Malaysia, the Union of Myanmar, the Republic of the Philippines, the Republic of Singapore, the Kingdom of Thailand and the Socialist Republic of Vietnam of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), … Do hereby commit to adhere to the ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS) Code of Practice.

MM.basis: ASEAN official accession date for Myanmar, from ASEAN’s own membership narrative.
MM.evidence_quote: Brunei Darussalam joined ASEAN on 7 January 1984, followed by Viet Nam on 28 July 1995, Lao PDR and Myanmar on 23 July 1997, and Cambodia on 30 April 1999, making up today’s ten Member States of ASEAN, or ASEAN-10.

MM.basis: IMF DSBB dates Myanmar’s e-GDDS metadata and NSDP, opened while checking the ASEAN five. Included because it is a real, country-named IMF obligation.

JP.basis: Replacement for the round-1 SNA-2008 edge that was actually quoting SDDS Plus. Cabinet Office / Statistics Bureau state that Japanese national accounts moved from 1993 SNA to 2008 SNA in 2016.
JP.evidence_quote: The Japanese National Accounts (JSNA) had been compiled based on the 1993 SNA (adopted by the United Nations in 1993) since 2000. The 2008 SNA (the latest international standard adopted by the United Nations in 2009) was introduced in 2016.

JP.basis: Replacement for the round-1 “observance report” edge. The 2024 SDDS Plus Annual Observance Report is the IMF’s own dated observance document for Japan; it is about SDDS Plus, not about SNA 2008 and not about the Statistics Act. Japan adhered to SDDS Plus on 18 April 2016.
JP.evidence_quote: Japan adhered to the SDDS Plus on April 18, 2016. … This report covers observance of the SDDS Plus undertakings by Japan in 2024, in the four dimensions of the SDDS Plus, as set forth in the SDDS Plus legal text

SD.sna-2008: Opened Sudan’s DSBB national-accounts metadata (last updated 1 July 2003). It states the compilation framework is still the 1968 SNA. No later official CBS or IMF quote was found adopting 2008 SNA. Null for sna-2008.
SD.imf-sdds: Sudan is not an SDDS subscriber. Null.

SL.sna-2008: No Statistics Sierra Leone or IMF page opened for this round actually says Sierra Leone compiles GDP on the 2008 SNA. UN National Accounts notes name Stats SL as compiler but do not, in the pages opened, assert 2008 SNA adoption. Null rather than infer.
SL.imf-sdds: Sierra Leone is e-GDDS with an NSDP, not an SDDS subscriber. Null.

IR.imf-sdds: No SDDS subscription. DSBB e-GDDS country page exists but is thin (“No coordinators exist.”). No IMF notice of formal withdrawal was found; also no notice of an active NSDP or a later revival. The August 2012 metadata posting is the only dated, citable edge.
IR.sna-2008: No official Statistical Centre of Iran page was opened that states 2008 SNA adoption. Null.

AF.imf-sdds: No SDDS subscription. No NSDP. No IMF notice that GDDS/e-GDDS participation was formally cancelled; also no evidence of a living dissemination program after the mid-2000s metadata posting.
AF.sna-2008: No official NSIA/CSO quote opened that states 2008 SNA adoption. Null.

YE.imf-sdds: No SDDS subscription. No NSDP. No IMF withdrawal notice found.
YE.sna-2008: No official CSO Yemen quote opened that states 2008 SNA adoption. Null.

SY.imf-sdds: No SDDS subscription. No NSDP. No IMF withdrawal notice found.
SY.sna-2008: No official Central Bureau of Statistics Syria quote opened that states 2008 SNA adoption. Null.

JP.statistics_act_as_sna_or_sdds_edge: Dropped. The Statistics Act (Act No. 53 of 2007) is a domestic legal framework for official statistics. Nothing in the Act text opened at soumu.go.jp / japaneselawtranslation.go.jp says that Japan implements SNA 2008 or observes SDDS/SDDS Plus. The previous quotes about SDDS Plus do not support an SNA-2008 or Statistics-Act edge.
